scope: The negative symmetric second difference of the actual SU(2) spatial Wilson action is controlled by the actual plaquette defects times the adjacent squared link-rotation displacements. If every spatial plaquette defect is at most delta, the bound is -32*delta*cost(q), with no volume factor. The temporal second difference is computed exactly as sum_e norm(q_e-1)^2*(2-norm(u_e-v_e)^2). For the already constructed exact middle Wilson law this yields action second difference at least beta*(4-eta_v-eta_w-32*delta)*cost(q). Under delta<=1/32 and squared endpoint-link distances<=1/2, it is at least 2*beta*cost(q), and the actual normalized log density has the opposite upper bound. These are pointwise finite-difference curvature estimates on the stated small-field sector, not global variance coercivity, spatial covariance decay, or control of the sector complement. All twelve full Clay obligations remain open. Exact antipodal endpoints cancel all middle-dependent temporal action, leaving beta*V plus a constant. On even spatial periods, every field and its pointwise antipode are related by a proved alternating central gauge transformation, so the actual physical endpoint source factor vanishes there. This exact cancellation supplies no uniform neighborhood estimate.

formal_results.antipodal_action: For every v,u, A_beta(v,-v;u)=beta*V(u)+4*beta*N_links. The pinning term becomes constant; squared distances to v and -v sum to 4 at each link.
formal_results.antipodal_physical_source: If 2 divides the spatial period, an explicit central alternating gauge sends every v to -v. Hence F(-v)=F(v) for all gauge-invariant F, and endpointWeight(v,-v)*(F(v)-F(-v))^2=0 exactly.
